data.name: Gildas
data.gender_notes: Gildas is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Celtic name Gild, meaning 'stranger' or 'foreigner'. This name was given to a 6th-century British monk and historian who wrote about the siege of his monastery by Saxon invaders. The name Gildas is a reminder of the hospitality and resilience of the early Christian community in the face of adversity. The name Gildas carries the meaning “Rule of the stranger” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Gildas usually hope their child will grow to embody rule of the stranger and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Welcomes the stranger, embraces the unknown.
data.etymology: Gildas belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Rule of the stranger.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Gildas total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_english.name: Gildas
in_english.meaning: Servant of gold or worker of gold
in_english.long_meaning: Gildas is a Christian Celtic name derived from Latin roots, specifically from the word 'gild' meaning 'servant of gold' or 'worker of gold'. This name was common among Celts and belonged to a 6th-century Christian priest. The name Gildas carries spiritual significance as a devoted servant of God, symbolizing humility and dedication. Historically, Saint Gildas was a prominent figure in Christian tradition, known for his piety and scholarship.

data.cultural_impact: Gildas is a Welsh name that carries the historical legacy of the early Christian community in Britain. Named after the monk and historian Gildas, who chronicled the siege of his monastery by Saxon invaders, this name represents the hospitality and resilience of the people during a time of great turmoil.
data.spiritual_significance: Gildas carries a deep spiritual significance as it is derived from the Celtic name Gild, meaning 'stranger' or 'foreigner'. This name serves as a reminder of the welcoming spirit of early Christianity towards those who were not part of their community. The name also symbolizes the strength and courage of the people in the face of adversity, inspiring us to open our hearts to those in need and to persevere through hardships.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Gildas: The radiant servant, illuminating the path to righteousness with unwavering dedication.

historical_references.reference: Gildas, a Briton monk and historian, is best known for his work 'De Excidio et Conquestu Britanniae' ('On The Ruin and Conquest of Britain'). In this work, he describes the devastation of Wales, Cornwall, and other parts of Britain by invading Saxon and Anglo-Saxon armies, and laments the moral decay of the British people. He is believed to have written this work around 540 AD.

Gildas is also mentioned by the Welsh historian Geoffrey of Monmouth in his 'Historia Regum Britanniae' ('History of the Kings of Britain'). According to Monmouth, Gildas was a contemporary of King Arthur and advised him to wage war against the Saxons. Monmouth's account, however, is considered to be a work of fiction rather than a historical fact.

His name is frequently referenced in academic and popular discussions of this period, and his legacy is celebrated in Welsh literature and folklore.
